key_insight: A Mamba-based language model combined with targeted data augmentation and experience replay (memory manipulation) produces property-optimized small molecules with far fewer training samples. This approach yields sample-efficient generative molecular design without needing massive new datasets.
problem_solved: Generative molecular design typically requires large datasets and many optimization steps to produce property-optimized compounds; this work addresses the low sample-efficiency and high compute/data costs of molecule generation and optimization.
method: Train a Mamba-based sequence model to generate molecular strings (SMILES/SELFIES) for de novo molecule creation.
Use data augmentation to expand and diversify training examples, improving generalization from limited data.
Apply experience replay / memory manipulation: store high-value generations and replay them during training to bias the model toward desirable properties.
impact: Enables faster, cheaper lead-generation and property optimization in molecular discovery workflows by reducing data and compute requirements; practical for labs and teams with limited experimental or compute budgets.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Mamba-based language model ingesting molecular tokens and outputting candidate molecules.
Pipeline flowchart: data augmentation → model sampling → scoring (properties) → experience replay buffer → retraining loop.
Performance plot: property score or reward vs. number of training samples comparing baseline vs. augmentation+replay (shows sample-efficiency gains).
Before/after molecule grid: example input molecules and generated optimized molecules with annotated property improvements.
paper_title: Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation
paper_authors: Jeff Guo, Junwu Chen, Anthony GX-Chen, Philippe Schwaller
